subject.title: Feature: Opt-in cross-channel visibility in TUI (mirror iMessage/Telegram activity)

question: Should OpenClaw add a default-off TUI cross-channel observer or mirror mode, and what transcript visibility boundary should it enforce across agents, sessions, channels, devices, and operators?
rationale: The source gap is real, but the requested capability changes transcript disclosure and may add public CLI/config surface, so automation should not choose the product and security boundary.

options.title: Read-only observer first
options.body: Add a default-off `openclaw tui --observe` style mode that only displays authorized activity for an explicit agent/session scope and defers bidirectional channel mirroring.

options.title: Full bidirectional mirroring
options.body: Allow TUI and channel messages to appear across surfaces, but require explicit delivery, authorization, redaction, docs, and upgrade policy before implementation.

options.title: No core mirror mode
options.body: Keep raw logs, existing session views, or a future activity timeline as the monitoring path and avoid cross-channel TUI transcript mirroring in core.

recommendation.title: Read-only observer first
recommendation.body: Add a default-off `openclaw tui --observe` style mode that only displays authorized activity for an explicit agent/session scope and defers bidirectional channel mirroring.

likelyOwner.reason: The remaining choice spans TUI UX, Gateway transcript visibility, and security defaults, and steipete has the strongest recent adjacent history signal among likely owners.
